title: Irregular indefinidos
topic: indefinido of ser/ir, tener, estar, hacer, poder, poner, venir, decir, querer, saber, dar
why: After the regular endings, this lesson gives you the irregular indefinidos of the verbs you need most to tell a story: ser and ir, tener, estar, hacer, poder, poner, venir, decir, querer, saber, dar, plus leyó, durmió, pidió. With them, you can finally talk about a vacation or a memorable day, while avoiding the typical mistakes (fuí, hico, dijieron).

Fui, fuiste, fue: ser and ir

Surprise: in the indefinido, ser and ir have exactly the same forms. The context tells you which verb it is, and in practice you'll almost never get it wrong. (English “to be” and “to go” are irregular in the past too: was, went.)

ser / irdarver
yofuidivi
túfuistedisteviste
él, ella, ustedfuediovio
nosotros, nosotrasfuimosdimosvimos
vosotros, vosotrasfuisteisdisteisvisteis
ellos, ellas, ustedesfuerondieronvieron
El sábado fui a Toledo. Fue un día increíble.On Saturday I went to Toledo. It was an amazing day.

In the first sentence, fui + a + place: it's ir. In the second, fue + adjective: it's ser.

Dar is an -ar verb, but in the indefinido it takes the -er / -ir endings, like ver: di, diste, dio. These very short forms have no written accent.

Classic mistake: writing “fuí” or “dió”. One-syllable forms don't take an accent: fui, fue, di, dio, vi, vio.

Tuve, estuve, hice: irregular stems

Many very common verbs change their stem in the indefinido, a bit like English “have → had”, “do → did”. The good news is that they all share the same endings, with no written accent: -e, -iste, -o, -imos, -isteis, -ieron.

poderpud-pudepudo

The traps

  • hizo is spelled with a z (not “hico”) to keep the sound.
  • decir gives dijeron, with no i: “dijieron” is a mistake.
  • No written accent: tuve, tuvo, hice, pudo, unlike regular verbs (hablé, habló).

English “I was”, “it was” has two Spanish versions: estuve for a place (estuve en Cádiz), fui / fue for identity or a judgment (fue fantástico, it was fantastic). It's the ser and estar rule you already know.

", "

Leyó, durmió, pidió: only in the third person

Some verbs are regular everywhere except in the third person singular and plural. For all the other persons, you conjugate normally.

TypeVerbsyoélellos
i → yleer, creer, oírleíleyóleyeron
o → udormirdormídurmiódurmieron
e → ipedir, repetir, servir, seguir, preferirpedípidiópidieron
Anoche dormí mal, pero mi hermano durmió diez horas.Last night I slept badly, but my brother slept ten hours.
En el restaurante pedí pescado y Marta pidió paella.At the restaurant I ordered fish and Marta ordered paella.

For leer, the i between two vowels becomes y: you write leyó, never “leió”. Same for creer (creyó) and oír (oyó).

Telling a memorable day

El verano pasado fuimos a Mallorca. Estuvimos diez días en un pueblo, hicimos muchas excursiones y un día vimos delfines. ¡Fue increíble!Last summer we went to Mallorca. We stayed ten days in a village, went on lots of excursions, and one day we saw dolphins. It was amazing!

Make a list of the ten most useful yo forms and repeat them out loud: fui, estuve, tuve, hice, pude, puse, vine, dije, quise, supe. Everything else follows from them.
